verdicts.reason: A uses a sensible left-to-right split (can left, quote right), but the quote runs across the edge of the background circle, the logo floats alone above the quote mark, and the attribution is tiny. B is close to a straight shrink of the original: the quote is small, the logo bottom-left is minuscule and the attribution is barely legible, but the composition, grouping and brand feel stay intact and nothing collides.

A sets an oversized logo in the top-right corner that competes with the content. The can is stranded at top centre, the quote is small and crosses the circle edge, and the bold attribution is almost as loud as the quote, so the hierarchy is inverted. B keeps a clean can-left, text-right banner with a proportionate logo, though the attribution is tiny and the text overlaps the circle edge.

Both use the same weak structure: the can sits at top centre with an unreadable label, the quote is small and runs across the circle edge, and the bold attribution rivals the quote. A's logo is oversized and crammed into the corner. B shrinks the logo to a more reasonable size, so it competes less, but the hierarchy and placement flaws remain.

A puts the can above the quote, so the reading order is image first and message second. The quote runs across the circle edge, and the bold attribution competes with it. B puts the quote first on a clean background, which reads better, but the can sits half on the circle edge in a way that looks accidental, the lower-left corner is empty, and the attribution is still too heavy.
